messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: Problem with to.dfs
parts:
I don't think it's trying to write there, I think it's trying to use that file as an executable, as in 

apc-2:RHadoop antonio$ /tmp 1
-bash: /tmp: is a directory

We have two possibilities: HADOOP_CMD is not properly set, fix that. Or it is properly set, but the hadoop installation went wrong for some reason. I would open a terminal and do a 
type -a hadoop
and a
echo $HADOOP_CMD
and if that is not set
echo $HADOOP_HOME
If they check right then I would investigate the differences between your interactive shell and the shell executed by rmr. It could be that variables are not set the right way. Mine are set in the .profile file, which I believe is read by most shells and then exported.
I hope this helps

Antonio

> small.ints = to.dfs(1:1000)

I have installed Hadoop in /home/me/usr/local/bin/hadoop, but I'm not sure why rmr wants to put small.ints there instead of HDFS. Maybe there is some Hadoop config file that needs to be changed? I have it running in pseudo-distributed mode right now. Thanks.
